scope.boundary: This packet identifies one exact type, descriptor, self-identifying candidate method table, its 26-slot base comparison, eight differing candidate methods, two triangle-list methods, one descriptor-referencing consumer, and one retained match-group record boundary. It does not prove a construction edge for the candidate table, name the nested 16-bit values, or prove runtime execution.

matchGroupBoundary.stringSearch: A case-insensitive canonical-image literal-string search for matchgroup, match group, and match returned 63 general matches and no match-group field-name or type-name literal.
matchGroupBoundary.readMethod: Candidate-table slot +0x10 is 0x823A3010, compared with base-table function 0x823F6B80. After the base call it reads the four-byte list length into object +0x44 and a one-byte presence value. When the presence value and +0x44 are nonzero, it allocates +0x44 times two bytes, stores that pointer at +0x48, and reads the packed list. It then reads a 16-bit outer count into +0x50, allocates +0x50 eight-byte records at +0x4C, and for each record reads a 16-bit nested count followed by count times two bytes into a buffer retained by that record's +0x4 pointer.
matchGroupBoundary.writeMethod: Candidate-table slot +0x1C is 0x823A3308, compared with base-table function 0x823F6BF8. After the base call it writes +0x44, a one-byte +0x48-presence value, and +0x44 times two bytes from +0x48 when present. It then writes +0x50 and, for each +0x4C record, its 16-bit count followed by count times two bytes from the record's +0x4 pointer.
matchGroupBoundary.recordShape: Object +0x50 is the retained outer count. Object +0x4C points to an array of eight-byte records; each record exposes a 16-bit nested count at +0x0 and a nested-value pointer at +0x4. The two bytes between them remain uninterpreted.
matchGroupBoundary.consumerMethod: Candidate-table slot +0x50 is 0x823F5430, compared with base-table function 0x827F16E0. It reads the packed triangle list at +0x48 and, only when +0x4C is non-null and +0x50 equals object +0x0C, uses each selected packed-list value to choose one eight-byte record. It iterates that record's nested 16-bit values as 12-byte strides into the buffer at object +0x24 while accumulating a computed three-float vector.
matchGroupBoundary.retentionResult: The read and write methods mirror the serialized outer-count, nested-count, and nested-u16 sequence immediately following the packed triangle list. The title retains that sequence in +0x50 and +0x4C records and one differing method consumes the retained nested values; the values are not discarded during this load path.
matchGroupBoundary.semanticLimit: The bounded methods prove storage shape and arithmetic use. They do not establish a semantic name for the nested values, prove that they are vertex or triangle indices, establish winding or visibility, or prove runtime execution.

conclusion: The current image contains an exact NiTriShapeData descriptor and a self-identifying 26-entry candidate method table. Slot +0x10 retains the serialized match-group outer count at object +0x50 and eight-byte nested-count and nested-u16-pointer records at +0x4C; slot +0x1C writes the mirror sequence, and slot +0x50 consumes those records. This closes the bounded retained-versus-discarded match-group contract. The candidate table still lacks a construction edge, the nested values retain no supported semantic name, runtime execution is unproved, and the broader Studio retained-array, material, texture, scene, and synthetic-fixture gates remain open; Model Viewer is not activated.
